q: Which of these is the regulator for the Indian mutual fund industry?
e: SEBI regulates mutual funds, AMCs, trustees, and distributors under SEBI Act 1992 + SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations. RBI handles banking, IRDAI insurance, PFRDA pensions.

o: Regulating mutual funds with statutory powers
Industry self-regulation, distributor licensing (ARN), investor education
e: AMFI = Association of Mutual Funds in India. Self-regulatory body. Issues ARNs to distributors, sets the Code of Conduct, runs investor awareness ('Mutual Funds Sahi Hai'), publishes industry data. SEBI is the actual regulator.

q: ELSS scheme must invest at least what % in equity to qualify for Section 80C tax benefit?
e: ELSS must hold minimum 80% in equity to qualify under Section 80C. The other 20% can be in debt or cash equivalents. The 3-year lock-in is the shortest among 80C instruments.

q: Performance ads for an MF scheme can be published only if the scheme is:
e: Performance ads require the scheme to be at least 1 year old. For schemes 1-3 years: annualised yields. For schemes >3 years: CAGR for 1, 3, 5 years and since inception (mandatory).

q: A Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) under PMLA must be filed with FIU-IND within:
e: Distributors and AMCs must file STRs to FIU-IND within 7 working days of detecting a suspicious transaction. Failure to file is a PMLA violation with significant penalties.

q: The single-company equity exposure limit per scheme (under SEBI MF Regulations) is:
e: Per scheme: maximum 10% of NAV in any single company's equity. Plus a separate cap on MF-wide ownership of any single company at 10% of voting rights.
